reader.title: Attempted lynching of Frank Wright
bases: A party of vigilantes took an accused horse thief from an officer and, in the Intelligencer's words, narrowly failed to lynch him (A4).
Wright 'narrowly escaped being lynched', so no one was killed; the vigilantes acted without authority over a horse-stealing accusation, but their number is not given (A4).
The arrest is reported independently by the Intelligencer and the Richmond Democrat (A1, A2), but the seizure by vigilantes appears only in one later Intelligencer item (A4).

summary.text: The attempted lynching of Frank Wright took place in western Missouri in late January 1888, when a party of vigilantes took Wright, an accused horse thief, from the Benton County officer who had arrested him near Mayview.
According to the Lexington Intelligencer, he narrowly escaped being hanged; the mob's part in the affair surfaced only in a single later clause of that paper's coverage of the Wright brothers.
The Intelligencer described five Wright brothers, three of whom, Tom, Riley and Frank, it called "pretty well known to be horse thieves" working between Benton and Lafayette counties.
In its telling, the brothers stole stock in one county and disposed of it in the other, swapping animals when they met halfway.
On Saturday, January 21, 1888, Frank Wright was arrested while visiting a brother who worked for J. R. Smith near Mayview.
A Benton County officer made the arrest with the help of John Pool, who stopped Wright with a shot over his head when he ran.
He was charged with horse stealing, and he was also suspected in the loss of a horse belonging to a Mr. Meyers near Mayview.
Neither early report mentions any mob.

On February 11, however, the Intelligencer recalled that Wright, accused of stealing a horse in Benton County and bringing it to Lexington for sale, "narrowly escaped being lynched by a party of vigilantes on the way, who took him from the officer."
The paper added that they "would certainly have stretched his neck, but" the surviving text breaks off there, so how he was saved is not recorded.
No arrest of any of the vigilantes and no outcome of Frank Wright's case appear in the coverage.
His brother Thomas was jailed at Lexington in early February on a horse-stealing charge brought by Amos Anson, and Riley was described as also wanted.
The arrest ran as a short item in the Intelligencer and in a "Missouri State News" column printed in the Richmond Democrat and the Iron County Register on February 2.
Only the Intelligencer mentioned the vigilantes, and it did so in passing within a long account of Thomas Wright's arrest, treating the brothers' guilt as known and offering no comment on the mob.
No paper stated the race of Wright or of the vigilantes.

accounts.label: Arrest reports
accounts.gist: Frank Wright was arrested near Mayview by a Benton County officer on a horse-stealing charge after running and being stopped by a shot over his head; nothing is said of a mob.

accounts.label: Intelligencer follow-up
accounts.gist: Two weeks later the Intelligencer recalled that Wright, on the way after his arrest, was taken from the officer by vigilantes who would have hanged him; the sentence breaks off before saying how he escaped.

framing.detail: The Intelligencer mentioned the vigilantes in one clause within a long item calling the Wright brothers 'pretty well known to be horse thieves', without comment on the mob.
The arrest ran as a plain news brief in a 'Missouri State News' column carried by the Richmond Democrat and the Iron County Register.

versions.value: Wright was suspected of stealing the Meyers horse near Mayview; the horse he rode was not the one he was charged with stealing
Riley Wright and the Meyers horse disappeared a few hours after Frank's arrest
Frank was arrested for stealing a horse in Benton County and bringing it to the Lexington area for sale

conflicts.note: The versions overlap rather than contradict, but they differ on which horse Frank was suspected of taking; the January 28 Intelligencer is closest to the arrest.

record_check.dossier: Arrest near Mayview, Lafayette County; the seizure happened 'on the way', county not stated. Benton is only where the alleged theft occurred and where the officer came from.
Arrest Saturday, January 21, 1888; seizure shortly after, exact date not given.

record_check.record: arrested in Benton county ... brought toward Lafayette county for sale
record_check.dossier: Arrested near Mayview (Lafayette County) for allegedly stealing a horse in Benton County and bringing it to the Lexington area for sale; taken from the officer 'on the way'.
The arrest also ran in the Intelligencer on January 28 and in a 'Missouri State News' column (Richmond Democrat, Iron County Register); only the February 11 Intelligencer mentions the vigilantes.

set_aside: Brother Riley ('Giley') Wright, charged with stealing horses from Moses Anson and Thos. Canfield, waived examination and was jailed; nothing on Frank.
Criminal court proceedings; search excerpt shows Riley Wright pleading guilty to grand larceny, three years; the re-read text printed is truncated before that entry. Nothing on Frank.
